passage.title: The Morning Check-In
passage.prompt: Explain one way the morning check-in could help students come to school on time. Use evidence from the passage to support your answer.
passage.text:
In a fictional middle school described here, many students arrived after the first bell, and some missed first period entirely. Teachers noticed that students who missed the start of the day often felt lost for the rest of the morning.

The school tried a morning check-in. Each day, an adult stood at the front door and greeted students by name. A table near the entrance offered a quick breakfast that students could carry to class. Students who had been absent the day before got a short note listing what they had missed.

After one semester, the attendance office reported that fewer students arrived late. Several students said that being greeted by name made them want to come to school, and one student said the breakfast meant she no longer had to choose between eating and catching the bus.

The program also had costs. Adults who greeted students had less time to prepare for their own classes. The breakfast table needed volunteers and supplies. Some students who rode late buses still arrived after the bell, so the check-in could not help them. The school decided to keep the program and to ask the bus company about earlier routes.
